messages:
lina: found something odd during a routine restore test: s3://backups/archives/2021-11/metadata_bundle.tar.gz contains a file named wrapped_vault_payloads.json and an attribute `vault_accessor_id` inside. looks like KMS-wrapped vault secrets. not sure if accessor corresponds to an active token. tagging @eng-security

tom: thanks. can you not try to auth with it. just list path and checksum. also note which KMS key id is embedded in the ciphertext header (if present).

lina: file path above. header shows key: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/legacy-ring/cryptoKeys/deploy-key. checksum sha256: a3f5...

rahul: OK. immediate scope: 1) check vault audit for any token auths by that accessor id; 2) query Cloud KMS key usage; 3) isolate the archive. I'll take 1 and 2.

infra-bot: automated: copied s3://backups/archives/2021-11/metadata_bundle.tar.gz -> s3://security-quarantine/auto/2021-11-metadata_bundle.tar.gz (acl: private).

lina: moved to quarantine. i also changed bucket lifecycle to prevent public read.

rahul: grep of vault audit: no auth attempts with that accessor. there are some earlier related auths around 2021-11-03 from infra-sa@redwood but not the specific accessor. cloudkms: 5 decrypts for deploy-key between 2021-11-02 and 2021-11-12 by legacy-deploy@redwood. no decrypts more recently.

tom: sounds similar to an old deploy then. treat as sensitive anyway. next steps: - revoke accessor if resolvable - revoke any tokens linked to that accessor/month - create new KMS key version and rewrap any active ciphertexts - run repo/backup scan for other occurrences of `wrapped_vault_payloads.json` and `vault_accessor` keys

sec-bot: alert: created incident INC-2026-042 (priority: P2) and started audit log tailing rule for deploy-key and related accessor patterns.

rahul: I requested operator privileges to list token accessors via Vault operator API. I was able to map accessor -> token lookup and found a matching accessor entry referencing a token that is now expired. lookup returned: "creation_time: 2021-11-03, ttl: 768h, expired: true". No active token. I still submitted a revoke-accessor for the accessor to be safe; response 204.

lina: I scanned the rest of the bucket and found 4 more archives with the same JSON file. all ciphertext-only. moving to quarantine as well. I'll annotate the incident ticket with the list.

tom: KMS plan: create key new-deploy-key in same keyRing, grant encrypt/decrypt to infra-bot and ops-sre, remove legacy-deploy SA. then run a limited rewrap for any ciphertexts with active metadata pointers (we have none). also create a Cloud IAM org policy to restrict decrypt to specific service accounts.

rahul: I also scanned CI logs for tokens being echoed; no hits for that accessor id or the filename. Searched github org for literal filename: found in 2 internal archived repos (both private), will request archival deletion and confirm object scan.

sec-bot: automated: scheduled SIEM rule: if any decrypt by deploy-key occurs, send to #eng-security and trigger runbook step.

lina: quick action item: add a backup pre-flight hook to run `jq` on archives and reject if `vault_token` or `vault_accessor` fields are present. filing a PR to infra.

tom: timeline: - revoke done (rahul) - KMS key created and restricted (tom) - quarantined artifacts moved (lina) - repo takedowns requested (rahul) - SIEM rule in place (sec-bot). target complete in 4 hours.

rahul: confirm: I did token revocation and double-checked vault: attempts to lookup the revoked accessor return 404. I also rotated a couple of leases that referenced the old tokens (job-runner leases).

lina: added notes to backup runbook: longer retention but auto-scan older than 30d. PR: infra#1547.

tom: posting final: no evidence of active compromise. still P2 because of exposed artifacts. we'll keep tailing for 72h per sec-bot. reopen if SIEM fires. :white_check_mark:
